reason: Filtering the blood starts the goal of separating small substances before recovering what the body needs.
expectation: I expect small substances, including glucose and waste, to pass through the filter while blood cells and large proteins stay in the blood.

alternatives.reason: The ureters would start the route to the bladder, but I want to follow filtration first.

effect: The filter lets useful glucose and water through along with wastes, so the recovery tube is the next step.
reaction: It makes sense now why filtering alone isn't enough.
reason: The recovery tube's picture shows useful substances returning to blood, directly advancing the filtration goal.
expectation: I expect glucose, some salts and much of the water to return to the blood, with wastes remaining in the tube.

alternatives.reason: The ureters would build the bladder route, but I want to finish following the filtered fluid first.

effect: Useful substances and much water return to blood, leaving waste-containing fluid to continue toward collection.
reaction: Seeing why the kidney takes materials back makes the two-stage process clearer.
reason: The ureters provide the tubes leading from the kidneys toward the bladder.
expectation: I expect the ureters to attach to the kidney pair, leaving the bladder connection to finish.

alternatives.reason: The bladder is also needed, but I want to build the route from the kidneys outward.

effect: The ureters now connect to the kidneys, leaving the bladder to complete the drainage route.
reaction: The downward arrows make the route easy to follow.
reason: This is the only available combination, and it connects the bladder to the ureters.
expectation: I expect the bladder to attach to the ureters so urine can collect there.

effect: The kidneys now have a continuous route through the ureters to the bladder; the remaining fluid still needs to be collected.
reaction: The drop tracing the route makes the connection clear.
reason: This is the only available combination and should complete the urine collection goal.
expectation: I expect the remaining waste-containing fluid to travel through the ureters and collect in the bladder as urine.

effect: The remaining fluid reaches the bladder as urine, completing the route while blood continues separately.
reaction: The final picture ties the filtering and drainage routes together clearly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Recovering useful substances after filtering was most worthwhile: it explained why the kidney doesn't just filter out waste.

leastWorthwhile.text: Attaching the bladder was straightforward and less engaging, though it completed the route.

surprise.text: The filter lets useful glucose and water through along with waste, so the body has to take some substances back.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless; the last combination was an obvious collection step rather than a discovery.

continue.text: I would continue for another chapter to see more connected body processes, although the final fittings were fairly predictable.
